question:
Rectangle \(ABCD\) is inscribed in a semicircle with diameter \(\overline{FE},\) as shown in the figure. Let \(DA=16,\) and let \(FD=AE=9.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The rectangle's width is \(DA=16\), so finding its height will give the area. Add the center \(O\) of the semicircle and join it to \(B\).

The diameter is \(FE=9+16+9=34\), giving radius \(OB=17\). The equal \(9\)-unit gaps on the two sides put \(O\) at the midpoint of \(DA\), so \(OA=8\).

Because \(AB\) is perpendicular to the diameter, \(\triangle OAB\) is a right triangle. Hence

\[
AB^2=17^2-8^2=289-64=225,\qquad AB=15.
\]

The rectangle's area is \(16\cdot15=\boxed{240}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\). Joining a circle's center to a known point on the circle turns the radius into a useful known length.
